data.title: STOCKS | Tech Stocks Slide as AI Sentiment Cools, Nvidia Loses $2.7 Trillion in a Month and a Half
data.description:
AI investment sentiment weakened as technology shares sold off, and Nvidia lost about $2.7 trillion in market value in a month and a half. According to Odaily, major U.S. stock indexes plunged, while Nvidia fell 14.01% on the 20th to a 52-week low. Its market capitalization dropped to about $3 trillion, placing it fourth among U.S. stocks after Alphabet overtook it. Nvidia's market value has fallen from a record high of about $5.77 trillion set on the 6th of the previous month, a decline equivalent to Amazon's entire market capitalization.

Despite Nvidia's strong results and Anthropic's public listing, investor sentiment did not recover and the tech-led selloff continued. On its second day of trading, Anthropic gave back most of the previous day's gains and closed down 8.50%, after briefly falling near its $83 IPO price. Major financial media have mainly attributed Nvidia's decline to weakening AI investment sentiment, the broader tech selloff and concerns about the company's accounting.

data.title: Bitcoin Core Releases 30.5 and 31.3 to Fix AI-Discovered Vulnerability
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Bitcoin Core released versions 30.5 and 31.3 to fix a medium-severity vulnerability that could cause nodes to stall. The flaw was discovered by Loupe, an AI scanning tool from Spiral. The discontinued 29.x branch is not covered by the fix and will not receive a patch.

data.title: China Uses Summits to Expand Influence as Xi Hosts Trump and Putin
data.description: According to CNBC, Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin at a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, after the leaders met at an APEC welcome banquet the previous evening. It was their first in-person meeting together. At the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting, Xi announced China would provide $20 million in support for the Asia Pacific region and advocated for an “Asia-Pacific community with a shared future.” Xi has hosted more than 40 heads of state so far this year, including at least eight around the APEC meetings in Shenzhen this week, after receiving over 60 state visits in 2025, according to official Chinese readouts. Tsinghua University researcher Jodie Wen said China’s engagement with major powers reflects its influence across the Global South and Eurasia, and that Beijing hopes to provide platforms for countries to discuss issues. EIU economist Yue Su said China uses multilateral platforms to expand its international influence and demonstrate its commitment to multilateralism, while focusing increasingly on economic benefits through trade, investment, financial connectivity and technology cooperation.

data.title: Analysts: Early Polar Vortex Breakdown Threatens Europe’s Depleted Gas Stocks
data.description: According to CNBC, an unprecedented early breakdown of the stratospheric polar vortex coinciding with a record-breaking El Niño has raised concerns about colder conditions and higher gas demand in Europe. European gas storage began the winter at its lowest level in more than a decade, and the International Energy Agency warned that low inventories and limited storage capacity in some importing countries could intensify competition for liquefied natural gas cargoes and put upward pressure on prices during periods of high demand. Wood Mackenzie gas analyst David Lewis said the combination of the early vortex breakdown and a strong El Niño has no historical precedent and could affect global gas demand. Rabobank senior energy strategist Florence Schmit warned that colder-than-expected weather could be difficult for Europe to manage, noting that gas storage withdrawals had been unusually strong over the previous two weeks. European gas prices reached 103.9 euros ($113.99) per megawatt hour in late October, their highest level since the 2022 energy crisis, while Dutch TTF futures for December delivery stood at around 87.28 euros on Friday afternoon.

data.title: Cyberattacks Expose Security Gaps at Europe’s Everyday Businesses
data.description: According to CNBC, attackers hit refrigeration systems in seven Swedish Coop stores in early November, after similar attacks on French supermarkets in October; Coop said security upgrades at the affected stores were scheduled for two days later and that the vulnerability has since been addressed. Sygnia handled 285% more incidents in October than a year earlier, CEO Guy Segal said, and some businesses seeking emergency assistance were turned away. Ahold Delhaize said a separate October cyberattack on its online operations and supply chain would reduce fourth-quarter sales by 200 million euros ($219 million).

data.title: The Kobeissi Letter Says Nasdaq 100's 10.4% Weekly Drop Was Rare in 40 Years
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing The Kobeissi Letter, the Nasdaq 100 fell 10.4% last week, a rare weekly decline over the past 40 years. Of 2,133 trading weeks, only 11 saw losses of the same magnitude or greater, representing 0.52%. Based on historical averages and volatility, the drop was equivalent to 3.27 standard deviations.

The Kobeissi Letter said market returns have fat tails, meaning extreme moves occur more often than a normal distribution would predict. Even accounting for that, it described the sell-off as historically rare and said volatility often returns when markets least expect it.

data.title: U.S. Startup GG Technologies Sues Apple in India, Alleging NameDrop Patent Infringement
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. startup GG Technologies has sued Apple in India, alleging that its NameDrop feature infringes the company’s patent. GG Technologies is seeking 15 billion rupees (about $161.86 million) and an injunction against the feature, which lets nearby devices exchange contact information.

The Santa Monica-based startup said it filed the case in India in October. Mediation, which began in April, failed in September; Indian commercial lawsuits generally require mediation before filing. GG Technologies also sued Apple in the United States in April over related patent claims. It filed a 781-page complaint with the Bombay High Court, seeking to bar Apple from selling or pre-installing iPhones and Apple Watches with NameDrop in India. No hearing has been scheduled. The company told TechCrunch it was seeking an injunction to prevent continued use of NameDrop as a native iOS feature.

GG Technologies launched its StayTouch app in 2019 to exchange contact details by bringing phones close together, without manual pairing. It first applied for a U.S. patent on the technology that year, applied for an Indian patent in 2021, and received the Indian patent in July 2024. Apple introduced NameDrop with iOS 17 in June 2023; it became available on iPhones later that year and on compatible Apple Watches through watchOS 10.1 in October.

The company was founded in 2018 by Gaurav Goel, an Indian Institute of Technology Delhi graduate and former Goldman Sachs investment banker. StayTouch supports iOS and Android. In the United States, the International Trade Commission opened a patent-infringement investigation into Apple in August after GG Technologies filed a complaint. The startup is seeking to block imports and restrict sales of allegedly infringing Apple devices. Apple did not respond to a request for comment. India is an increasingly important consumer market and manufacturing base for Apple outside China. The company is expanding its retail stores in India, where iPhones account for less than 10% of smartphone shipments.

data.title: Vietnam Lawmakers Approve Changes to Speed Land Clearance, Project Development
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Vietnam’s National Assembly passed amendments to land laws aimed at speeding site clearance and unblocking property and infrastructure projects. The government is seeking to achieve its multiyear target for double-digit economic growth.

data.title: Adam Kobeissi Says Bitcoin Has Erased All Gains Since Trump's Election
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing The Kobeissi Letter founder Adam Kobeissi, sentiment-driven liquidity tightening in stock and gold markets on November 21 was spreading to crypto. Crypto liquidations of leveraged positions totaled $2.3 billion over the past 24 hours, marking the 13th-largest liquidation event on record. Since U.S. President Donald Trump won the 2024 election, the crypto market has surrendered all its gains, with the cumulative change reaching negative $2.3 trillion, Kobeissi said. He added that liquidity squeezes pose risks for 24/7 markets and that liquidity must recover before markets can bottom.

data.title: Anthropic IPO Shares May Have Favored Heavy Claude Users, Investors Suspect
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, some investors suspect Anthropic favored heavy users of its Claude model in allocating IPO shares, though the company also distributed large allocations to major institutions including Citadel. More than half of the shares reportedly went to existing investors, including Altimeter Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures. About 60% of institutions that ordered shares received none, while BlackRock reportedly sought about $10 billion worth and received roughly half that amount.

Anthropic shares rose more than 30% above the offering price when trading began Thursday, then closed up 17%. On Friday, they fell as much as 15%, briefly trading just 5 cents above the offer price, before closing down 8.5% at $88.91, still 7% above the offering price. The company’s market value fell by about $109 billion. Nvidia, Meta and Oracle also declined, and the Nasdaq market lost a combined $4 trillion in value. Anthropic’s IPO and concurrent placement raised more than $100 billion; the IPO allocation was valued at $81 billion.

The allocation drew criticism from investors who said they received fewer shares than requested or none at all. One hedge fund manager also questioned the underwriters’ decision on the opening time and price. Some current and former employees were permitted to sell about 300 million shares immediately, worth roughly $26 billion at the offering price, rather than face the usual lockup. Anthropic said Friday morning that the underwriters had fully exercised the IPO’s 15% greenshoe option. About 300 million more shares are due to become tradable on December 15.

The selloff also weighed on plans by rival OpenAI, which plans to go public next year and is pursuing a large funding round at a post-money valuation of $1.25 trillion. Meanwhile, some San Francisco AI workers focused on a claim by an Anthropic mathematician that Claude had solved a 167-year-old Millennium Prize problem.

data.title: Predict.fun Adds Prediction Event on Amazon’s Year-End 2026 Market Cap
data.description:
Predict.fun has added a prediction event on Amazon’s market capitalization at the end of 2026. According to Odaily, settlement will be based on Amazon’s public market capitalization at the close of regular trading on the final trading day of 2026, calculated by multiplying the official closing price of its shares on the primary exchange by the total shares outstanding at that time.

The calculation may include all classes of outstanding shares, using applicable conversion ratios; shares without conversion rights will be counted as disclosed unless official company documents specify otherwise. The share count will be determined from company filings or disclosures. If the market capitalization falls exactly on a boundary between two ranges, it will be assigned to the higher range.

If Amazon acquires or merges with another entity and remains the parent company, the same calculation will apply. If Amazon is acquired, ceases to be the surviving parent after a merger, or is no longer an independent entity before the period ends, settlement will use the public market capitalization reached before the transaction is completed and will exclude transaction, acquisition or merger consideration. Settlement will rely on official exchange data and publicly disclosed share counts.
